Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Gentoo Media

A quarter that confirms the August diagnosis rather than changes it: the cost base and 41% EBITDA margin are intact and the December bond cliff is gone, but the revenue engine is still shrinking (€20.8m/~$22.7m, -9% YoY, seventh consecutive decline) and FY26 guidance was cut for the third time in three months because operators resisted the commercial re-terms meant to convert record deposits into revenue. The price of the balance-sheet fix is control: the Juroszek family now owns ~56–59% of the equity and holds all of the residual ~€57.5m (~$62.9m) of debt at EURIBOR+7.50%.

Acroud AB

A weak quarter that was then made almost irrelevant by Brazil: revenue -20% to EUR 10.4m (~$11.4m) and adj. EBITDA -30% to EUR 1.0m (~$1.1m) on a 52% collapse in SaaS EBITDA, while a Brazilian provisional measure banning fixed-odds betting removes the ~EUR 1.4m (~$1.5m) of Jan–Aug EBITDA — roughly 40-45% of the 9M group total on our arithmetic — and forced the July 2026-28 targets to be suspended. Galaxy Gaming

A clean recurring-revenue quarter wrapped in a messy P&L: recurring revenue net of royalties hit a record $7.96m (+9.7% YoY, 99.9% of sales) and Core recurring accelerated to +11.4%, but adj. Grandstand

Q3-26 was a sequential improvement (revenue +7% QoQ to $40.3m, adj. EBITDA +31% QoQ to $10.0m, margin 20%→25%) that still missed the Street by ~3–4% on revenue and fell well short of the company's own plan, forcing a FY26 guidance cut to ~$157m / ~$37m from $165–170m / $45–50m — the entire shortfall sits in consumer-facing brands (international SEO/casino affiliate and OddsJam subscriptions) while B2B (OpticOdds >50%, Grandstand Partners) grows. Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Arizona

Arizona's sixth NFL September delivered a handle of $836.7m (-1.7% YoY) but a far better revenue print: gross receipts +18.5% to $65.2m on a 7.8% hold, promo deductions down to 49% of gross, taxable receipts +68% to $33.0m and state fees +70% to $3.3m. The market is a 99.7%-mobile, FanDuel/DraftKings duopoly (61.5% of handle) operating under one of the lowest effective tax regimes in the US (~5% of gross) — which is precisely why the Governor's 45% tier for ≥$75m-handle operators and the criminal case against Kalshi make the next 12 months a regulatory, not a demand, story.

Market report · OCTOBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Wyoming

October 2026 confirms Wyoming as a small, mature, DraftKings-led, mobile-only sportsbook market whose growth has stalled: handle fell 7.3% YoY to $22.6m, GGR fell 12.4% to $2.47m and state tax fell 9.0% to $177,882, even as lifetime handle crossed $1bn and 2026 YTD remains +6.9%. The regime is among the cheapest and simplest in the US (untethered $100k five-year permit, 10% of net proceeds with promo deductions), but the political direction is prohibitionist on casino-style product: the Select Committee on Gaming has sent a felony ban on online casino and sweepstakes operation to the 2027 session rather than a regulatory framework.

Market report · FY 2026 · Confidence medium

South Africa

South Africa's regulated gambling market set a record R84.46bn (~$5.12bn) GGR in FY2025/26 (+13.4%), but the growth is a single engine — online sports betting (R55.77bn, +25%) licensed province-by-province and taxed at ~6.5% of GGR plus VAT. The rules are now moving against the grain of that growth: the SCA has shut the bookmaker 'casino-game' loophole, Treasury wants a 20% national online GGR tax with the design due in the Feb-2027 Budget, advertising norms are drafted, and a site-blocking tender is live — while online casino stays illegal and an estimated majority of online play sits offshore. Attractive scale, deteriorating rule-set.

Mississippi

Mississippi remains a $2.4bn-a-year, 100% land-based, low-tax (≈12% of GGR) casino market that is flat at the top line and structurally leaking sports-betting demand to mobile-enabled neighbours: October AGGR was $198.4m (-0.2% YoY; YTD -0.7%) while retail sports handle fell for a 15th straight month to $36.2m (-7.8%). The 2026 session once again saw the House pass statewide mobile wagering (100–11) and the Senate kill it in committee; with 2027 an election year and the Lt Governor publicly opposed, the operator read-through is a stable but ex-growth retail franchise with a binary, politically gated mobile option.

Market report · 2026 · Confidence medium

Lithuania

Lithuania's regulated gambling market is compounding at mid-teens rates — 9M-26 GGR €229m (~$250.5m), +14% — almost entirely on online slots, with remote now 78% of GGR and retail shrinking 6.5%. But the state is about to take a much larger cut and a much tighter grip: a 22%→36% progressive GGR tax proposed from July 2027, a full advertising ban from January 2028 and a mandatory player card with cashless venues from 2029. The commercial window is real but narrowing, and it belongs to scale incumbents; for a newcomer the only credible routes are acquisition of a licensee or B2B supply.

Market report · 2025/26 · Confidence medium

Great Britain

Great Britain remains the largest fully-regulated online gambling market in Europe and is still growing — FY2025/26 GGY £17.5bn (~$23.4bn), +4.4%, with online casino (+£736m, ~$986m) delivering effectively all of the growth while online betting and betting shops went backwards. But the state is now taking a far larger share: Remote Gaming Duty doubled to 40% of GGY from 1 April 2026, remote betting duty rises from 15% to 25% in April 2027, a statutory levy (~1.1% of online GGY) started in April 2025, and enforcement — local inspections +29%, £26m of new anti-illegal-gambling funding, FATF-driven AML focus — is visibly tightening. For B2Tech the market offers scale, legal certainty and mature payments, but post-tax online casino economics now favour only the largest, most efficient operators, and the regulatory direction of travel is unambiguously restrictive.

Massachusetts

Massachusetts is a mature, two-operator-dominated online sportsbook market (DraftKings + FanDuel = 74% of handle, 82% of taxable revenue) where volume has stalled (October handle $874.1m, -2.0% YoY; YTD +1.5%) but hold expansion keeps revenue and tax creeping higher (taxable SWR $73.6m, +3.3%; YTD $685.1m, +5.7%). The land-based base is shrinking (casino GGR $90.3m, -6.8%, strike-hit Encore -11.7%), iGaming is parked until 2027, and the live regulatory risk is binary: a Senate bill proposing a 51% online tax plus prop/in-play bans sits in Ways & Means, while the SJC has yet to rule on whether Kalshi's sports contracts are unlicensed wagering.

Washington DC

October 2026 was the District's largest month on record by handle ($95.76m) but growth has stalled at +0.9% YoY, hold is flat at 8.8%, and tax take fell 1.7% as volume shifted toward the 20%-taxed venue books. The bigger story is regulatory: B26-0656 (online casino at 25% GGR plus 4% of assessments, sweepstakes folded into licensing, gambling age to 21) cleared committee 3-1 on 18 Nov and must survive two full-Council readings before the Council period closes in mid-December. For a would-be entrant, DC is a ~$90m-GGR, seven-brand, FanDuel-dominated market where the 30% Class C tax and $2m licence make a mobile-only sportsbook entry marginal; the credible angles are B2B supply or an iGaming licence if the bill lands.

Market report · 9M 2026 · Confidence medium

Arizona

Arizona is a ~$9bn-handle, mobile-only-in-practice sports-betting market growing at low single digits (9M-26 handle $6.54bn, +3% YoY) with the cheapest fiscal terms of any large US state — 10% on receipts net of promos, an effective ~6–7% of gross win. The two things that matter for an entrant are (i) access, because the 20-licence cap means you need a tribal or pro-team partner, and (ii) tax risk, because the Governor's 45% large-operator proposal is unenacted but not dead. No online casino, and none coming without a compact rewrite.

Market report · 2023-2025 · Confidence medium

European Union

The ECA-commissioned GCI study sizes the EU27 online betting-and-gaming marketplace at €128.0bn (~$140.2bn) GGR in 2025, of which only €36.5bn (~$40.0bn, 28%) sits with locally licensed operators and €91.6bn (~$100.3bn, 72%) with operators lacking the national licence required — a cumulative €224.8bn (~$246.2bn) "illegal" take and €56.3bn (~$61.6bn) of forgone tax over 2023–25. The regulated base is corroborated by EGBA/H2 (EU27+UK online €47.9bn in 2024, implying ~€36–37bn ex-UK) and is growing high-single digits, but the black-market figure is 5–8x the competing Euromat/Regulus (€12bn net, ~25%) and H2 (~€18bn, ~27%) estimates and should be treated as an upper bound. For an operator the EU remains 27 separate, expensive (avg €1.1m initial fee, 24% avg GGR tax) national regimes with no passporting; the actionable opportunities are the markets re-regulating in 2026–28 (Finland, Austria, Ireland) and the better-channelised Nordic and Southern European markets, not an "EU-wide" play.

Market report · 2026 · Confidence medium

Chile

Chile in late-2026 is two markets moving in opposite directions: a mature, SCJ-regulated land-based casino sector shrinking in real terms (9M-26 GGR CLP 401.9bn / ~$395m, -7.9% real for the 22 concession casinos; visits -11%) and a large, wholly unlicensed online market that the courts, Subtel and the tax authority are now squeezing (79 domains DNS-blocked since September; 19% VAT levied on offshore gaming margin with no licence attached). The Senate Economy Committee voted 3-1 on 9 Nov 2026 to replace the government's licensing bill with a ban or a Polla/Lotería monopoly, while the Kast government counters with a 22%-of-GGR licence regime and a total advertising and bonus ban; the choice between those two paths, due to start being resolved at the committee vote on 1 Dec 2026, is the single swing factor for any entrant.
